title: 糸 (Ito — Thread)
description:
One of the most celebrated Japanese ballads of the 20th century. Written and performed by 中島みゆき (Nakajima Miyuki), released on the 1992 album『EAST ASIA』. The song uses the metaphor of the vertical thread (縦の糸) and horizontal thread (横の糸) of a woven cloth to express the idea that two people, living separate lives moving in perpendicular directions, are woven together by fate into something stronger and more beautiful than either thread alone.

The song became a cultural touchstone after it was used in the 2020 film『糸』(Ito), and has been covered by dozens of Japanese artists. It is frequently performed at weddings and graduation ceremonies.

The spelling 仕合わせ (instead of the usual 幸せ) is deliberate — Nakajima uses the archaic form that literally means 'to be drawn together by fate', reinforcing the thread/weaving metaphor.

For learners: This is rich N2 material. Key grammar and vocabulary: 縦の糸 / 横の糸 (vertical/horizontal thread — metaphor you must understand to follow the whole song), 仕合わせ vs 幸せ (homophone with different kanji; the archaic 仕合わせ = 'fate bringing people together'), なぜ (why — rhetorical, repeated throughout), 逢う (逢 is the literary kanji for 'to meet' — same sound as 合う but more poetic), 布 (ぬの — cloth/fabric — the payoff of the weaving metaphor), 縒り合わせる (よりあわせる — to twist/spin together), 誰かのために生きる (living for someone else — N3 phrase but used in literary context), ひとつの布 (a single piece of cloth). The repeated rhetorical なぜ questions and the extended metaphor sustained across the whole song are what push this to N2.
